title: nothing re-drives an open issue, so a fixed-but-open row reads as live and its cost lands on whoever cites it: two worked instances in one day
body:
**NOTHING RE-DRIVES AN OPEN ISSUE, SO A ROW WHOSE DEFECT HAS BEEN FIXED STAYS OPEN AND READS AS LIVE.** The register records a defect at the moment it was found and has no mechanism -- verb, gate or instrument -- that ever asks whether it is still true. **A fixed-but-open row is invisible by construction: it looks exactly like a real one, and its cost lands on whoever reasons FROM it rather than on whoever left it open.**

## Population, measured 2026-09-04

    228 issues total
    147 OPEN, 81 closed
    open by month created:  2026-08 -> 118,  2026-09 -> 29
    open at high or critical severity: 53

## TWO WORKED INSTANCES ON ONE DAY, AND NEITHER WAS FOUND BY LOOKING FOR THIS

**1. `0223` REASONED FROM `0090` AND `0151` IN WRITING.** Its text concluded that a junk row created by the title-positional defect *cannot be corrected or retitled; it can only be closed*, sourced explicitly to those two. **Both had been fixed** -- `intent issues edit` takes `--body` and `--title` and both write, driven with a positive control. **Three open issues, one expired premise, and none of the three noticed.** The cost was a real constraint on a real disposition decision, believed because it was sourced.

**2. A SCHEMA RUNG WAS PRICED AGAINST A VARIANT THAT ALREADY EXISTED.** `0063` claims `WpStatus` has no `Cancelled` variant, so a descoped work package can never be closed. vc joined that to a live hazard -- the migration ladder 13->17 takes **no backup on any rung** -- and asked for it to be sized before starting. **`WpStatus` has had `Cancelled` since `85a0ed235`, with `wp cancel` and `wp reinstate` both shipping.** The sizing question was well-formed, the hazard it named is real, and the join could not fire.

**In both cases the instrument was sound and the SUBJECT had moved.** That is the same shape as a stale binary or a stale figure, one level up: **a citation inherits the cited claim's truth at citation time and never updates, and a reference is worse than a bare claim because it reads as sourced.**

## WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, AND THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE FINDING

**NO RATE IS CLAIMED AND NONE SHOULD BE INFERRED FROM THIS ROW.** Three of the four open issues driven on 2026-09-04 turned out to be already fixed (`0090`, `0151`, `0063`; `0223`'s own defect is still live). **n=4, and the selection is the OPPOSITE of random** -- those four were driven precisely because each was blocking some other piece of work, which biases hard toward rows that other work still points at. **Three-of-four is not a rate, it is four anecdotes with a shared cause**, and treating it as a proportion of 147 would be exactly the arithmetic error this estate keeps recording.

**A TRIAGE SWEEP IS NOT PROPOSED HERE.** Re-driving 147 rows is L+ at least, most of them are legitimately open, and deciding to spend that is a scope call. **This row exists to name the mechanism and record its two instances, not to request the work.**

## What a remedy would have to answer, if one is ever wanted

**The cheap direction is not re-driving rows; it is making a CITATION checkable.** When `0223` cites `0090`, nothing links them and nothing notices when `0090`'s status changes. **An issue that cites another issue is the case where staleness is both most likely to matter and most mechanically detectable** -- the citing row is the one that gets believed. Whether that is worth a link field, a lint, or nothing at all is a design call this row deliberately does not pre-empt.
